title: What Are Public Domain Books? A Complete Guide
description: Learn what public domain books are, how they become free to read, and where to find classic literature, scientific works, and open educational resources online.
content:
## What Does Public Domain Mean?

A **public domain** book is a creative work that is not protected by intellectual property laws like copyright, trademark, or patent. This means the work belongs to the public — anyone can read, share, download, print, or even adapt it without asking for permission or paying fees.

## How Books Enter the Public Domain

There are three main ways a book becomes public domain:

| Method | Description | Example |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| Copyright expiration | Copyright lasts for a limited time (author's life + 70 years in most countries) | Works by Jane Austen, Charles Dickens |
| Published before copyright | Books published before modern copyright laws existed | Shakespeare's plays, Plato's works |
| Dedicated by author | Authors can voluntarily release works into the public domain | Some modern open-licensed books |

> "The public domain is not just a collection of old works — it is the raw material from which new culture is built."

## Where to Find Public Domain Books

Here are the best sources for free public domain books:

| Source | Number of Books | Best For |
|--------|----------------|----------|
| **Project Gutenberg** | 70,000+ | Classic literature, general reading |
| **Open Library** | Millions | Rare and modern public domain works |
| **Internet Archive** | Millions | Scanned books, historical texts |
| **Google Books** | Varies | Academic and out-of-print books |

### Project Gutenberg Classics

Project Gutenberg is the oldest digital library, founded in 1971. It offers over 70,000 free ebooks in formats like HTML, EPUB, Kindle, and plain text. Every book is thoroughly reviewed for copyright status before being added.

## Why Read Public Domain Books?

- **Completely free** — no subscriptions, no payments
- **Legally shareable** — send books to friends, print copies, use in classrooms
- **Rich educational value** — foundational texts in philosophy, science, literature, and history
- **Multiple formats** — read online, on e-readers, or listen as audiobooks

## Start Reading Today

On **BitLibrary**, you can discover public domain books from Project Gutenberg, Open Library, and Internet Archive all in one place. Search by author, category, or subject, and read directly in your browser with a clean, focused reading interface.

title: Nepal Education Curriculum: CDC Textbooks for Classes 1-12
description: An overview of the Nepal education system, CDC curriculum textbooks for classes 1 through 12, and how students and teachers can access Nepali educational resources online.
content:
## Overview of Nepal's Education System

The **Curriculum Development Centre (CDC)** under the Government of Nepal develops the national curriculum for school education. The system is structured into two main levels:

| Level | Grades | Age Group |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Basic Education | 1 to 8 | 5–13 years |
| Secondary Education | 9 to 12 | 14–17 years |

## Subjects Covered by CDC

CDC textbooks cover the following core subjects across all grades:

| Subject | Grades | Description |
|---------|--------|-------------|
| **Nepali** | 1–12 | Nepali language, grammar, and literature |
| **English** | 1–12 | English language and communicative skills |
| **Mathematics** | 1–12 | Arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and statistics |
| **Science** | 1–12 | Physics, chemistry, biology, and environmental science |
| **Social Studies** | 1–12 | History, geography, civics, and economics |
| **Health** | 1–10 | Physical health, nutrition, and personal safety |
| **Hamro Serofero** | 1–3 | Our surroundings — integrated environmental learning |

## How to Access CDC Textbooks

Traditionally, students had to buy printed textbooks from bookstores. Now, digital access is transforming Nepali education:

1. **BitLibrary** — Browse CDC curriculum books by class and subject for free online reading
2. **CDC Official Website** — Download PDF versions of official textbooks
3. **CEHRD Portal** — Access teacher guides and supplementary materials
4. **School Distribution** — Many government schools distribute textbooks for free

## What Are Free Audiobooks?

Free audiobooks are audio recordings of books that are available to stream or download at no cost. Most free audiobooks come from **public domain** texts — works whose copyright has expired — which volunteers record and make available for everyone.

## The Best Source: LibriVox

**LibriVox** is the largest provider of free public domain audiobooks. Here's what you need to know:

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Total titles | 15,000+ |
| Languages | 100+ (mostly English) |
| Readers | All volunteers |
| Format | MP3, M4B, streaming |
| Cost | Completely free |
| License | Public domain |

### How LibriVox Works

Volunteers from around the world record chapters of public domain books. Each audiobook is:

- **Coordinated** by a dedicated book coordinator
- **Proof-listened** for quality control
- **Cataloged** with full metadata and chapter markers
- **Released** into the public domain

title: Open Digital Library vs Traditional Library: Benefits and Differences
description: Compare open digital libraries with traditional libraries. Learn about the benefits of online book access, digital reading, and how platforms like BitLibrary bridge the gap.
content:
## The Evolution of Libraries

Libraries have been centers of knowledge for centuries. Today, they exist in two complementary forms: **traditional physical libraries** and **open digital libraries**. Each has unique strengths, and together they provide unprecedented access to human knowledge.

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Feature | Traditional Library | Open Digital Library |
|---------|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Access hours** | Limited (usually 9 AM–8 PM) | 24/7/365 |
| **Location** | Physical building needed | Anywhere with internet |
| **Book availability** | One copy per person at a time | Unlimited concurrent readers |
| **Searchability** | Card catalog / staff help | Full-text search across millions of books |
| **Late fees** | Yes | None |
| **Cost** | Free membership (usually) | Completely free |
| **Book condition** | Wear and tear | Perfect every time |
| **Accessibility** | Varies by location | Equal access worldwide |
| **Community** | In-person events, story time | Online communities, forums |
| **Rare books** | Physical archives | Scanned digital copies |

## The Best of Both Worlds

### What Traditional Libraries Excel At

- **Community programs** — story time for kids, book clubs, workshops
- **Librarian expertise** — personalized recommendations and research help
- **Physical spaces** — quiet study areas, meeting rooms, makerspaces
- **Special collections** — rare manuscripts, local history archives
- **No internet needed** — accessible to people without connectivity

### What Digital Libraries Excel At

- **Instant access** — find and read a book in under 10 seconds
- **Vast catalogs** — millions of titles at your fingertips
- **Built-in reading tools** — adjustable fonts, bookmarks, highlights, search
- **Accessibility features** — screen readers, large text, dyslexia-friendly fonts
- **No geographic limits** — someone in rural Nepal can access the same books as someone in New York

## How BitLibrary Bridges the Gap

BitLibrary combines the best aspects of both worlds:

> **It offers the warmth and discoverability of a curated library with the speed and accessibility of modern digital tools.**

| BitLibrary Feature | Inspired By |
|--------------------|-------------|
| Category browsing | Library shelves |
| Search with suggestions | Librarian expertise |
| Reading interface | Quiet reading room |
| Save and bookmark | Your personal bookshelf |
| AI summaries | Reference desk help |
| Open source | Public ownership model |

## The Future of Libraries

The future is not digital OR physical — it's both. Libraries are adapting by offering digital lending alongside physical collections. Open digital libraries like BitLibrary complement traditional libraries by making knowledge accessible to anyone with an internet connection, while physical libraries continue to serve as vital community hubs.

title: Nepali Literature: Notable Books, Authors, and Reading Resources
description: Explore Nepali literature, famous Nepali authors, classic Nepali books, and where to find Nepali language reading materials online for free.
content:
## A Rich Literary Tradition

Nepali literature has a rich and diverse tradition spanning more than two centuries. From epic poetry to modern novels, Nepali writers have made significant contributions to world literature while maintaining a distinctly Nepali voice.

## Famous Nepali Authors

| Author | Born–Died | Known For | Notable Work |
|--------|-----------|-----------|--------------|
| **Laxmi Prasad Devkota** | 1909–1959 | Poetry, essays | *Muna Madan* |
| **Parijat** | 1937–1993 | Novels, stories | *Shirishko Phool* |
| **Bhupi Sherchan** | 1937–1989 | Poetry | *Ghumne Mech Mathi Andho Manchhe* |
| **Banira Giri** | 1946–2021 | Poetry, novels | *Karas* |
| **Ramesh Kshitij** | 1955– | Stories, novels | *Suna Nara* |
| **Narayan Wagle** | 1966– | Novels, journalism | *Palpasa Cafe* |

## Classic Nepali Books You Should Read

### 1. Muna Madan by Laxmi Prasad Devkota
A narrative poem about a man who leaves his wife and mother to go to Tibet for work. It is one of the most beloved works in Nepali literature.

### 2. Shirishko Phool by Parijat
Widely considered the greatest Nepali novel, this story explores love, loss, and social injustice through the metaphor of a withered flower.

### 3. Ghumne Mech Mathi Andho Manchhe by Bhupi Sherchan
A powerful poetry collection that critiques social and political issues in Nepal with sharp wit and vivid imagery.

### 4. Palpasa Cafe by Narayan Wagle
A novel set during the Nepalese Civil War, exploring love, conflict, and the human cost of war.

## Nepali Literature by Genre

| Genre | Notable Works |
|-------|---------------|
| **Poetry** | Muna Madan, Ghumne Mech Mathi Andho Manchhe |
| **Novels** | Shirishko Phool, Palpasa Cafe, Karas |
| **Short Stories** | Stories by Ramesh Kshitij, Indra Bahadur Rai |
| **Drama** | Plays by Abhi Subedi, Balkrishna Sama |
| **Essays** | Works by Laxmi Prasad Devkota, BP Koirala |

- **Nepali curriculum textbooks** (Nepali subject for classes 1–12)

- **Nepali literature** in the Nepali Literature category

> Nepali literature offers a window into the Nepali soul — its struggles, joys, beauty, and resilience.
